observations:
LM2 Torah 112 is a single-sentence aphorism — among the shortest entries in Likutay Moharan. The complete text reads: 'Regarding strengthening oneself so that a person should not fall in his mind because of the multitude of flaws and corruptions that he corrupted through his actions, [the Rebbe] answered and said: If you believe that they can corrupt, believe that they can repair.'

The teaching contains no bechina language (no 'X הוא בחינת Y', no 'X נקרא Y', no conceptual equivalences). There is a rhetorically symmetrical pair — קִלְקוּל (corruption/ruin) and תִּקּוּן (repair/rectification) — but these stand in a logical-causal relationship, not a bechina (shared-nature) relationship. The Rebbe does not say 'corruption is an aspect of repair' or equate their essential natures; he argues that the same faith-capacity (אֱמוּנָה) that acknowledges the reality of ruin must equally acknowledge the reality of repair. This is an eitza-type argument by analogy: the belief in one implies the belief in the other. Neither concept is defined as an aspect of the other.

A new package requires 3 or more concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. That condition is entirely unmet here. There are no candidate nodes, no equating language, and no ontological topology to map.

Conclusion: NO_NEW_PACKAGES. The dataset correctly has zero entries for reference 1112, and there is nothing in the source text that warrants adding any.
